items.validationError: jonah-1-calling: reading companion requires human approval
items.payloadProbe: Nineveh is the city Jonah is told to visit. The opening gives a command, but does not yet tell us what Jonah thinks of it.

items.validationError: jonah-1-escape: reading companion requires human approval
items.payloadProbe: Watch the repeated movement away: Jonah goes to Joppa, finds a ship, and pays his fare. The verse describes his departure without explaining his motive.

items.validationError: jonah-1-storm-wind: reading companion requires human approval
items.payloadProbe: The sailors act while Jonah sleeps. Notice how the captain addresses someone who has withdrawn from the danger they share.

items.validationError: jonah-1-storm-lots: reading companion requires human approval
items.payloadProbe: Jonah identifies himself by the God he fears. Read that declaration beside what he has already done.

items.validationError: jonah-1-storm-sea: reading companion requires human approval
items.payloadProbe: Before throwing Jonah into the sea, the sailors try to row to land. Their hesitation is part of the story too.

items.validationError: jonah-1-depths: reading companion requires human approval
items.payloadProbe: The account moves from the open sea to confinement. Let the change in scale settle before continuing.

items.validationError: jonah-2-prayer: reading companion requires human approval
items.payloadProbe: Jonah’s prayer moves between being overwhelmed and being heard. Read slowly; its images of descent and return belong to the prayer itself.

items.validationError: jonah-2-shore: reading companion requires human approval
items.payloadProbe: The chapter ends with Jonah on dry land. The verse gives no speech from him. Pause here before the command returns.

items.validationError: jonah-3-return: reading companion requires human approval
items.payloadProbe: The command comes a second time. Compare this opening with the first: the destination is the same, but Jonah’s direction changes.

items.validationError: jonah-3-mercy: reading companion requires human approval
items.payloadProbe: The people, the king, and even the animals enter the account. Notice the king’s uncertainty, and what the narrator says God sees.

items.validationError: jonah-4-anger: reading companion requires human approval
items.payloadProbe: Here Jonah names his reason for fleeing. Read his explanation beside the mercy he has just received and the mercy the city receives.

items.validationError: jonah-4-shade: reading companion requires human approval
items.payloadProbe: A vine brings relief, then withers. The conversation turns toward what Jonah cares for, and what he did not bring into being.

items.validationError: jonah-4-question: reading companion requires human approval
items.payloadProbe: This is the book’s final verse. No reply from Jonah follows. There is room to sit with the question without resolving it.
